original_question: If A_K denotes the largest continued-fraction coefficient of 2^K sqrt(2) for K = 1, 2, ..., what are the sharp growth bounds for B_L = max_{K<=L} A_K?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Open Problem 8, stated as a preparatory question for Open Problem 7 on the discrepancy of the concrete Halton–Kronecker sequence with van der Corput component in base 2 and Kronecker component {n√2}. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact sequence from the paper, uses the same quantities A_K and B_L, and asks for the same kind of result: sharp growth bounds for the maximal continued-fraction coefficient along 2^K√2. This is precisely the content of Open Problem 8 as introduced immediately after Open Problem 7. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
missing_details: The paper places this question in the narrower context of analyzing the discrepancy of the concrete Halton–Kronecker sequence ((x_n,{n√2})) with x_n the van der Corput sequence in base 2; Open Problem 8 is explicitly presented as prework for Open Problem 7, not as a free-standing continued-fraction problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
K and L should be stated to range over positive integers, and the asymptotic regime should be made explicit as L → ∞. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

To make the problem mathematically stand-alone and nontrivial, one should specify that A_K refers to the non-initial partial quotients in the regular/simple continued fraction of 2^K√2 (equivalently, after removing the integer part). This is implicit from the discrepancy context: if the initial coefficient were included, then A_K would be dominated by ⌊2^K√2⌋ and the problem would become trivial. This clarification is an inference from the nearby context rather than an explicit sentence in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))

The draft does not specify that the continued fraction is the ordinary regular continued fraction; the paper simply says 'continued fraction coefficients,' so this standard convention should be spelled out in a stand-alone reformulation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
refined_question: For the concrete Halton–Kronecker sequence ((x_n,{n√2}))_{n≥0}, where x_n is the van der Corput sequence in base 2, let A_K denote, for each positive integer K, the largest non-initial partial quotient a_j (j ≥ 1) in the regular continued fraction expansion of 2^K√2, and define B_L := max_{1≤K≤L} A_K. What are the sharp upper and lower bounds for the growth of B_L as L → ∞?
justification: The draft is aimed at Open Problem 8 in Section 3: the paper asks for sharp bounds on the growth of B_L built from the largest continued-fraction coefficients associated with 2^K√2, and it introduces this as a necessary preliminary step toward Open Problem 7 on the discrepancy of the specific Halton–Kronecker sequence using the base-2 van der Corput sequence and {n√2}. Because the paper treats this as a nontrivial auxiliary Diophantine-approximation problem, a complete stand-alone formulation should make explicit that one is tracking the non-initial partial quotients of the regular continued fraction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1407.2380))
